title: Surprise regulatory fine on bank reputation and stock value

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Event Study (Market Model)**

This is a classic event study design to measure abnormal returns around surprise regulatory fine announcements.

**Approach:**
1. **Estimation window [−10, −2]:** Estimate market model parameters (α, β) for each bank using the pre-event window to establish "normal" expected returns.
2. **Event window [−1, +1]:** Compute abnormal returns (AR = ret − (α̂ + β̂ × mkt_ret)) and cumulate them into CAR[−1,+1] for each bank.
3. **Test for reputational damage:** Compare CAR against zero (standard event study test) and against −fine_ratio (to assess whether the stock price decline exceeds the direct financial cost of the fine, implying reputational spillover damage).

**Key assumptions:**
- The market model estimated in [−10, −2] captures normal return-generating process (no anticipation/contamination in estimation window).
- The fine announcement is a "surprise" — not anticipated by the market before day −1.
- No confounding firm-specific events in the [−1, +1] window.
- Returns are cross-sectionally independent (or we cluster appropriately).

## 2. R Code

```r
# ============================================================
# Event Study: Surprise Regulatory Fine & Bank Stock Returns
# ============================================================

library(data.table)

# --- Read data ---
dt <- fread("experiments/exp_b/data/s17_data.csv")

cat("=== Data Overview ===\n")
cat("N rows:", nrow(dt), "\n")
cat("N banks:", uniqueN(dt$stock_id), "\n")
cat("Event days:", sort(unique(dt$event_day)), "\n\n")

# Check if fine_ratio exists in data
has_fine_ratio <- "fine_ratio" %in% names(dt)
cat("fine_ratio column present:", has_fine_ratio, "\n\n")

# --- Step 1: Estimate Market Model in [-10, -2] for each bank ---
est_window <- dt[event_day >= -10 & event_day <= -2]

# OLS for each stock: ret_i,t = alpha_i + beta_i * mkt_ret_t + epsilon
models <- est_window[, {
  fit <- lm(ret ~ mkt_ret)
  list(alpha_hat = coef(fit)[1],
       beta_hat  = coef(fit)[2],
       sigma_hat = summary(fit)$sigma,
       r_sq      = summary(fit)$r.squared,
       n_obs     = .N)
}, by = stock_id]

cat("=== Estimation Window Market Model Summary ===\n")
cat("Mean alpha:", round(mean(models$alpha_hat), 6), "\n")
cat("Mean beta (estimated):", round(mean(models$beta_hat), 4), "\n")
cat("Mean R²:", round(mean(models$r_sq), 4), "\n")
cat("Mean residual sigma:", round(mean(models$sigma_hat), 6), "\n\n")

# Also check provided beta vs estimated beta
if ("beta" %in% names(dt)) {
  provided_betas <- dt[, .(beta_provided = first(beta)), by = stock_id]
  comp <- merge(models, provided_betas, by = "stock_id")
  cat("Correlation(estimated beta, provided beta):", 
      round(cor(comp$beta_hat, comp$beta_provided), 4), "\n\n")
}

# --- Step 2: Compute Abnormal Returns in Event Window [-1, +1] ---
event_window <- dt[event_day >= -1 & event_day <= 1]

# Merge model parameters
event_window <- merge(event_window, models[, .(stock_id, alpha_hat, beta_hat, sigma_hat)], 
                      by = "stock_id")

# Abnormal returns using estimated parameters
event_window[, AR := ret - (alpha_hat + beta_hat * mkt_ret)]

# Also compute AR using provided beta (assuming alpha=0 as is standard with provided beta)
event_window[, AR_provided_beta := ret - (beta * mkt_ret)]

# --- Step 3: Compute CAR[-1, +1] for each bank ---
car_by_stock <- event_window[, .(
  CAR = sum(AR),
  CAR_prov = sum(AR_provided_beta),
  n_days = .N
), by = stock_id]

# Merge fine_ratio if available
if (has_fine_ratio) {
  fine_info <- dt[, .(fine_ratio = first(fine_ratio)), by = stock_id]
  car_by_stock <- merge(car_by_stock, fine_info, by = "stock_id")
}

cat("=== CAR[-1, +1] Summary (Estimated Market Model) ===\n")
cat("Mean CAR:", round(mean(car_by_stock$CAR), 6), "\n")
cat("Median CAR:", round(median(car_by_stock$CAR), 6), "\n")
cat("Std CAR:", round(sd(car_by_stock$CAR), 6), "\n")
cat("Min CAR:", round(min(car_by_stock$CAR), 6), "\n")
cat("Max CAR:", round(max(car_by_stock$CAR), 6), "\n")
cat("% Negative:", round(mean(car_by_stock$CAR < 0) * 100, 1), "%\n\n")

# --- Step 4: Statistical Tests ---

# Test 1: Is mean CAR significantly different from zero?
t_test_zero <- t.test(car_by_stock$CAR, mu = 0)
cat("=== Test 1: H0: CAR = 0 ===\n")
cat("Mean CAR:", round(t_test_zero$estimate, 6), "\n")
cat("t-statistic:", round(t_test_zero$statistic, 4), "\n")
cat("p-value:", format.pval(t_test_zero$p.value, digits = 4), "\n")
cat("95% CI: [", round(t_test_zero$conf.int[1], 6), ",", 
    round(t_test_zero$conf.int[2], 6), "]\n\n")

# Cross-sectional t-test (BMP test)
N <- nrow(car_by_stock)
bmp_t <- mean(car_by_stock$CAR) / (sd(car_by_stock$CAR) / sqrt(N))
cat("BMP cross-sectional t-stat:", round(bmp_t, 4), "\n")
cat("BMP p-value (two-sided):", format.pval(2 * pt(-abs(bmp_t), df = N - 1), digits = 4), "\n\n")

# Non-parametric: Wilcoxon signed-rank test
wilcox_zero <- wilcox.test(car_by_stock$CAR, mu = 0, alternative = "two.sided")
cat("Wilcoxon test p-value (CAR ≠ 0):", format.pval(wilcox_zero$p.value, digits = 4), "\n\n")

# Sign test
n_neg <- sum(car_by_stock$CAR < 0)
sign_test_p <- binom.test(n_neg, N, p = 0.5)$p.value
cat("Sign test: ", n_neg, "/", N, " negative CARs, p-value:", 
    format.pval(sign_test_p, digits = 4), "\n\n")

# Test 2: Is CAR < -fine_ratio (reputational damage beyond direct cost)?
if (has_fine_ratio) {
  car_by_stock[, excess_loss := CAR - (-fine_ratio)]  # CAR + fine_ratio; if < 0 => repn damage
  # Equivalently: CAR + fine_ratio < 0 means stock dropped more than fine amount
  
  cat("=== Test 2: H0: CAR + fine_ratio >= 0 (no reputational damage) ===\n")
  cat("Mean fine_ratio:", round(mean(car_by_stock$fine_ratio), 6), "\n")
  cat("Mean (CAR + fine_ratio):", round(mean(car_by_stock$excess_loss), 6), "\n")
  
  t_test_rep <- t.test(car_by_stock$excess_loss, mu = 0, alternative = "less")
  cat("t-statistic:", round(t_test_rep$statistic, 4), "\n")
  cat("p-value (one-sided, < 0):", format.pval(t_test_rep$p.value, digits = 4), "\n")
  cat("95% Upper bound:", round(t_test_rep$conf.int[2], 6), "\n\n")
  
  cat("% of banks where CAR < -fine_ratio:", 
      round(mean(car_by_stock$excess_loss < 0) * 100, 1), "%\n\n")
  
  # Reputational multiplier: how many times the fine is the total loss?
  car_by_stock[, rep_multiplier := ifelse(fine_ratio > 0, -CAR / fine_ratio, NA)]
  cat("=== Reputational Multiplier (-CAR / fine_ratio) ===\n")
  cat("Mean multiplier:", round(mean(car_by_stock$rep_multiplier, na.rm = TRUE), 2), "\n")
  cat("Median multiplier:", round(median(car_by_stock$rep_multiplier, na.rm = TRUE), 2), "\n\n")
}

# --- Step 5: Day-by-Day Average AR (for the full window) ---
cat("=== Day-by-Day Average Abnormal Returns ===\n")
daily_ar <- dt[, .(mkt_ret_mean = mean(mkt_ret)), by = event_day]

# Merge estimation parameters to full dataset
dt_full <- merge(dt, models[, .(stock_id, alpha_hat, beta_hat)], by = "stock_id")
dt_full[, AR := ret - (alpha_hat + beta_hat * mkt_ret)]

daily_stats <- dt_full[, .(
  mean_AR = mean(AR),
  se_AR = sd(AR) / sqrt(.N),
  t_AR = mean(AR) / (sd(AR) / sqrt(.N)),
  n = .N
), by = event_day][order(event_day)]

daily_stats[, cum_AR := cumsum(mean_AR)]

print(daily_stats[, .(event_day, 
                       mean_AR = round(mean_AR, 6), 
                       t_AR = round(t_AR, 3),
                       cum_AR = round(cum_AR, 6))])

# --- Step 6: Robustness Checks ---
cat("\n=== Robustness Check 1: Using Provided Beta (alpha = 0) ===\n")
t_test_prov <- t.test(car_by_stock$CAR_prov, mu = 0)
cat("Mean CAR (provided beta):", round(t_test_prov$estimate, 6), "\n")
cat("t-statistic:", round(t_test_prov$statistic, 4), "\n")
cat("p-value:", format.pval(t_test_prov$p.value, digits = 4), "\n\n")

# Robustness: Wider event window [-1, +3]
cat("=== Robustness Check 2: Wider Event Window [-1, +3] ===\n")
event_wide <- dt_full[event_day >= -1 & event_day <= 3]
car_wide <- event_wide[, .(CAR_wide = sum(AR)), by = stock_id]
t_wide <- t.test(car_wide$CAR_wide, mu = 0)
cat("Mean CAR[-1,+3]:", round(t_wide$estimate, 6), "\n")
cat("t-statistic:", round(t_wide$statistic, 4), "\n")
cat("p-value:", format.pval(t_wide$p.value, digits = 4), "\n\n")

# Robustness: Narrow event window [0, +1]
cat("=== Robustness Check 3: Narrow Event Window [0, +1] ===\n")
event_narrow <- dt_full[event_day >= 0 & event_day <= 1]
car_narrow <- event_narrow[, .(CAR_narrow = sum(AR)), by = stock_id]
t_narrow <- t.test(car_narrow$CAR_narrow, mu = 0)
cat("Mean CAR[0,+1]:", round(t_narrow$estimate, 6), "\n")
cat("t-statistic:", round(t_narrow$statistic, 4), "\n")
cat("p-value:", format.pval(t_narrow$p.value, digits = 4), "\n\n")

# Robustness: Event-day only
cat("=== Robustness Check 4: Event Day Only [0] ===\n")
event_day0 <- dt_full[event_day == 0]
t_day0 <- t.test(event_day0$AR, mu = 0)
cat("Mean AR[0]:", round(t_day0$estimate, 6), "\n")
cat("t-statistic:", round(t_day0$statistic, 4), "\n")
cat("p-value:", format.pval(t_day0$p.value, digits = 4), "\n\n")

# Robustness: Check pre-event CAR[-10,-2] should be ~0 (placebo)
cat("=== Robustness Check 5: Pre-Event Placebo CAR[-10, -2] ===\n")
pre_event <- dt_full[event_day >= -10 & event_day <= -2]
car_pre <- pre_event[, .(CAR_pre = sum(AR)), by = stock_id]
t_pre <- t.test(car_pre$CAR_pre, mu = 0)
cat("Mean CAR[-10,-2]:", round(t_pre$estimate, 6), "\n")
cat("t-statistic:", round(t_pre$statistic, 4), "\n")
cat("p-value:", format.pval(t_pre$p.value, digits = 4), "\n")
cat("(Should be ~0 if market model is well-specified)\n\n")

# --- Final Summary ---
cat("=" , rep("=", 59), "\n", sep = "")
cat("FINAL SUMMARY\n")
cat("=" , rep("=", 59), "\n", sep = "")
cat("Number of banks: ", N, "\n")
cat("Mean CAR[-1,+1]: ", round(mean(car_by_stock$CAR) * 100, 3), "%\n")
cat("t-stat (CAR = 0): ", round(bmp_t, 3), "\n")
if (has_fine_ratio) {
  cat("Mean fine_ratio:   ", round(mean(car_by_stock$fine_ratio) * 100, 3), "%\n")
  cat("Mean excess loss:  ", round(mean(car_by_stock$excess_loss) * 100, 3), "%\n")
  cat("Reputational mult: ", round(mean(car_by_stock$rep_multiplier, na.rm = TRUE), 2), "x\n")
}
cat("Conclusion: CAR is ", ifelse(t_test_zero$p.value < 0.05, "significantly", "not significantly"),
    " different from zero at 5% level.\n")
if (has_fine_ratio) {
  cat("Reputational damage (CAR < -fine_ratio): ",
      ifelse(t_test_rep$p.value < 0.05, "YES (significant)", "NO (not significant)"),
      " at 5% level.\n")
}
```

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study with CAR decomposition: financial cost vs. reputational component
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: CAR exceeds fine/mktcap ratio, confirming reputational damage beyond monetary penalty
_ground_truth.main_effect: CAR ≈ −3.5%; reputational component ≈ −1.5% above direct cost
